root_cause.text: `dw_dp_bind()` in the DW-DP DRM bridge driver had incorrect error-handling control flow, allowing execution to continue after `drm_bridge_attach()` failure and failing to clean up the non-devm `drm_dp_aux_register()` resource on subsequent error paths, with an additional bad return-value use for `platform_get_irq()` errors.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret) dev_err_probe(...);` to `if (ret) { dev_err_probe(...); goto unregister_aux; }`, adds `drm_dp_aux_unregister(&dp->aux);` at a shared cleanup label for failures after AUX registration, and fixes the IRQ path from `if (dp->irq < 0) return ERR_PTR(ret);` to `ret = dp->irq; goto unregister_aux;`, showing the original bug was missing early exit plus incomplete cleanup in `dw_dp_bind()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: `dw_dp_bind()` in `drivers/gpu/drm/bridge/synopsys/dw-dp.c` had broken error handling after `drm_dp_aux_register()`/`drm_bridge_attach()` and other init steps, so failures could fall through without cleanup (leaking the AUX registration) and one path returned the wrong error value after `platform_get_irq()`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `goto unregister_aux;` after failures from `drm_bridge_attach()`, `phy_init()`, `devm_add_action_or_reset()`, `platform_get_irq()`, and `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, then calls `drm_dp_aux_unregister(&dp->aux)` in the new cleanup label; it also fixes `if (dp->irq < 0) { ret = dp->irq; goto unregister_aux; }` replacing the նախկինly incorrect `return ERR_PTR(ret);`, and the commit message explicitly states that `drm_dp_aux_unregister()` was missing on all those error paths and that `drm_bridge_attach()` failure lacked a return.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence and consistency are mostly good, but one key detail is wrong: the proposed root cause says the wrong return after `platform_get_irq()` was `ERR_PTR(ret)`, but the patch actually shows `return ERR_PTR(ret);` only after `devm_add_action_or_reset()` and `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, while the `platform_get_irq()` bug is specifically `if (dp->irq < 0) { ret = dp->irq; goto unregister_aux; }` replacing `return ERR_PTR(ret);` with `ret = dp->irq`. Also, the evidence claims the patch “adds `goto unregister_aux;` after failures from `drm_bridge_attach()`, `phy_init()`, `devm_add_action_or_reset()`, `platform_get_irq()`, and `devm_request_threaded_irq()`,” which is true, but the root cause should explicitly mention the missing return after `drm_bridge_attach()` continuing execution as a separate control-flow bug, not just “broken error handling.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure `dw_dp_bind()` cleans up AUX registration on all post-registration failures and returns the correct IRQ lookup error.
intent_record.what: The function `dw_dp_bind()` was changed so that several failure paths now jump to a new `unregister_aux` label instead of returning immediately. A new cleanup block was added at the end of the function that calls `drm_dp_aux_unregister(&dp->aux)` and then returns `ERR_PTR(ret)`. The bridge attach, PHY init, `devm_add_action_or_reset`, IRQ lookup, and IRQ request error paths were all updated to use this shared cleanup path, and the IRQ lookup failure now explicitly assigns `ret = dp->irq` before branching.
intent_record.how: On any failure after the AUX channel has been registered, the function now properly unregisters the AUX device before exiting, preventing stale registration and potential resource leaks. It also fixes the IRQ lookup error path so the returned error reflects the actual IRQ acquisition failure instead of incorrectly reusing an unrelated `ret` value. Runtime behavior is otherwise unchanged on the success path.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable control flow and resource-handling issues in `dw_dp_bind()`. After `drm_bridge_attach()` the code only logs on failure: `ret = drm_bridge_attach(...); if (ret) dev_err_probe(dev, ret, "Failed to attach bridge\n");` and then continues executing `dw_dp_init_hw(dp);`, `phy_init(dp->phy);`, and IRQ setup instead of returning on attach failure. This matches the described incorrect error-handling flow.

It also shows the non-devm AUX registration not being cleaned up on later failures: `ret = drm_dp_aux_register(&dp->aux); if (ret) ... return ERR_PTR(ret);` registers a resource, but there is no corresponding unregister on later error paths after this point.

Finally, the bad return-value use for `platform_get_irq()` is present: `dp->irq = platform_get_irq(pdev, 0); if (dp->irq < 0) return ERR_PTR(ret);` returns `ERR_PTR(ret)` instead of the actual IRQ error (`dp->irq`), so the function uses the wrong value on failure. None of these issues are corrected in the shown code.
